{{short description|American college basketball season}} {{Use American English|date=March 2026}} {{Use mdy dates|date=August 2023}} {{Infobox NCAA team season |mode=Basketball |year= 2014–15 |team= Florida Gators |image=Florida Gators wordmark.svg |image_size= 250 |conference=Southeastern Conference |short_conf=SEC |CoachRank= |APRank= |record= 16–17 |conf_record= 8–10 |head_coach=[[Billy Donovan]] |hc_year= 19th |asst_coach1= Rashon Burno |asst_coach2= [[Matt McCall (basketball)|Matt McCall]] |asst_coach3= [[John Pelphrey]] |stadium= [[O'Connell Center]] |mvp = |champion= |conf_champ = |conf_champ_result = |bowl= |bowl_result= }} {{2014–15 Southeastern Conference men's basketball standings}} The '''2014–15 Florida Gators men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of Florida]] in the sport of [[college basketball|basketball]] during the [[2014–15 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The Gators competed in the [[Southeastern Conference]] (SEC). They were led by nineteen-year head coach [[Billy Donovan]], and played their home games in the [[O'Connell Center]] on the university's [[Gainesville, Florida]] campus. They finished the season 16–17, 8–10 in SEC play to finish in a tie for eighth place. They advanced to the quarterfinals of the [[2015 SEC men's basketball tournament|SEC tournament]] where they lost to Kentucky. Gator non-participation in a postseason tournament had been 17 years before. The Gators' 63.7 points-per-game had been their lowest during Billy Donovan's 19-year coaching tenure. After the season, Donovan accepted an offer to coach the [[National Basketball Association|NBA]]'s [[Oklahoma City Thunder]]. He would leave the Gators as the regular season games' winningest head coach in the program's history and while at the helm coached the Gators to more NCAA tournament appearances, and more SEC championships, than the combined totals of all the other head coaches in the program's history.{{Citation needed|date=September 2017}} ==Previous season== {{main|2013–14 Florida Gators men's basketball team}} The Gators finished the 2013–14 season as the SEC regular-season champions with an overall record of 36–3, 18–0 record in conference play, the first SEC team to ever accomplish the feat, after the SEC re-expanded to an 18-game regular-season schedule prior to the [[2012–13 Southeastern Conference men's basketball season|2012–13 season]].{{cite news |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2014/03/09/sports/ncaabasketball/florida-trounces-kentucky-to-finish-undefeated-in-sec.html?_r=0 |title=Gators Overwhelm Wildcats to Cap SEC’s First 18-0 Season |last1=Spousta |first1=Tom |date=March 8, 2014 |newspaper=[[The New York Times]] |access-date=March 9, 2014}} In doing so, the Gators won their seventh SEC regular season championship, and their third in four seasons. The Gators beat the [[2013–14 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team|Kentucky Wildcats]] 61–60 to claim the SEC Tournament championship. As a No. 1 seed in the [[2014 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2014 NCAA tournament]]'s South Region, Florida won its four tournament games, defeating 16-seed [[2013–14 Albany Great Danes men's basketball team|Albany]], 8-seed [[2013–14 Pittsburgh Panthers men's basketball team|Pittsburgh]], 4-seed [[2013–14 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|UCLA]] and 11-seed [[2013–14 Dayton Flyers men's basketball team|Dayton]].
